whyItMatters: Interactive access followed by sensitive cloud activity is one of the clearest indicators that a session was operationally abused rather than used for routine maintenance.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may open an interactive Session Manager shell and then pivot into secrets access, role chaining, IAM changes, or snapshot creation shortly afterward.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This sequence is a practical post-compromise pattern because SSM provides the hands-on keyboard access needed to inspect hosts, extract credentials, or trigger follow-on cloud actions.
threatContext.whyItMatters: CloudTrail does not show shell commands, so the strongest proxy is the sequence of interactive access followed by sensitive cloud APIs.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, defenders may see the session and the later API calls as unrelated events rather than a single intrusion chain.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail management events for SSM
AWS CloudTrail management events for Secrets Manager, KMS, STS, IAM, EC2 and related services
loggingRequirements: StartSession and follow-on management events must be ingested in the same analytics environment.
Actor identity should be normalized across direct and assumed-role sessions.
Ordered short-window correlation must be available in the detection engine.
limitations: CloudTrail cannot prove what happened inside the shell.
Simple counts grouped by ARN do not prove sequence.
Some legitimate admin sessions are followed by sensitive API activity, so target and actor context remain important.

rawToNormalized.notes: Sensitive API action after the session

enrichment.description: Normalize direct and assumed-role identities so the session actor can be matched to follow-on cloud activity.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Improves correlation fidelity across role hops.

enrichment.description: Classify the host accessed by the session and its likely secrets or privilege exposure.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Explains why later activity after the session is important.

enrichment.description: Group later actions into secrets access, role chaining, IAM mutation, and snapshot or collection behavior.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Makes post-session abuse sequences clearer and easier to triage.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This rule should model a short-window post-session sequence: an actor opens an SSM session and then performs sensitive cloud actions soon afterward. The detector should require ordered correlation and stable actor identity rather than matching either side independently.
conditions: first eventSource equals ssm.amazonaws.com and eventName equals StartSession
second event is a sensitive cloud API by the same actor or normalized session identity
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Require ordered sequence, not loose co-occurrence. 2. Normalize direct and assumed-role identities. 3. Escalate further when the target host is sensitive or the actor is unauthorized for interactive access.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when interactive Session Manager access is followed quickly by sensitive cloud activity from the same operator identity.

simulationCommand: aws ssm start-session --target i-0abc123 && aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id ExampleSecret

quality.falsePositiveRate: Low-Medium depending on admin workflows and actor-target context

deployment.scheduling: Best in near-real-time because the session-to-abuse window is short and actionable.
considerations: This is one of the strongest SSM abuse detections in the family.
Ordered correlation and stable identity normalization are critical.
